objective: Gate the open-water curve of the Potsdam Propeller Test Case VP1304, that is thrust coefficient KT, torque coefficient KQ and open-water efficiency against advance ratio J, using steady incompressible RANS with a moving reference frame, against the SVA Potsdam open-water tables, with the gate specification naming WHICH of that report's four differently corrected tables is the reference
rationale: This is the one naval item that can proceed today, and the docket's stated reason for it is wrong in both halves. Why it can proceed: the case is single phase, submerged and steady, with no free surface, so it does not inherit the F7 dam break ladder block that stops every hull case. And the reference data is genuinely open. The SVA Potsdam report is free with attribution and carries full J, KT, ten KQ and efficiency tables plus polynomial fits, which is stronger than the KCS propeller, whose geometry is available but whose open water data was searched for and not found openly, and far stronger than the Wageningen B series, whose regression coefficients were searched for and are not openly obtainable. Now the correction. The docket says this reuses the F8 moving reference frame machinery, the naval turbine. Checked against F8's own dictionaries and record rather than repeated, both halves fail. First, F8 is not naval and not a propeller: it is a WIND turbine in AIR at kinematic viscosity 1.4805e-05, and its steady moving reference frame branch is closed on evidence three ways with zero gated numbers, so there is no validated result to inherit. Second, its blade surface is a fixed 68 MB, 330,950 triangle S809 wind blade with no generator anywhere in the repository, so a five bladed high skew marine propeller is 100 percent new geometry work, not an edit. Third, and this is the trap: the sign convention is INVERTED, because a propeller absorbs torque where a turbine extracts it, and that is precisely the error class that cost F8 three riders on its own gate. What genuinely transfers is dictionaries and process discipline. That is real and it is worth having, but it is not what reusing the machinery prices at, and this proposal is priced from scratch rather than by analogy because of it
gate: Declared before any mesh exists. Reference, and this clause is the point: SVA Potsdam Report 3752 contains FOUR differently-corrected open-water tables which disagree materially, so the pre-registration must name WHICH table by its correction, with the page and the correction's own description quoted, and hash the source PDF. A gate citing SVA 3752 without that has named a document containing four answers, which is the same defect class F7a_REGATE_SPEC.md was written to retire. Stations: advance ratios frozen before the first solve, spanning the tabulated range and including the design point. Metric definition pinned in advance: the thrust and torque integration patches and whether hub and shaft are included, the rotation-axis and sign conventions, the reference diameter and revolution rate, and the non-dimensionalisation of KT, KQ and eta_O written as formulae not as names. Averaging window and transient-rejection rule declared in advance, with the settling test explicit. Three-valued verdict per docket B2: PASS if max deviation across the frozen advance ratios is inside the declared band for both KT and KQ on two mesh rungs, with the fine rung not worse; FAIL, reported as a result, if outside with settled histories; NO VERDICT if the settling test fails, which is what the nearest comparable case in this lab actually returned
cost_basis: Priced from scratch against F8's MEASURED throughput, not against F8's estimate and not by analogy to its scope. F8's rotor measured 0.54 to 0.60 core seconds per iteration at 230,135 cells, taken from its own wall times and rank counts. Note the caution that forces this construction: F8's own proposal estimated 6 core minutes and the item cost 47.7, an eight times overrun, so any figure built on F8's ESTIMATE inherits that error and this one is built on its measurement instead. Its record also carries a 0.145 core seconds per iteration figure that is inconsistent with every other number in the same document, and that figure is not used. Scaling 0.57 core seconds per iteration linearly in cell count: a propeller sweep at 600,000 cells runs about 1.49 core seconds per iteration, so 3,000 iterations is about 74 core minutes per advance ratio. Priced as one coarse feasibility point at about 37, a seven point curve at about 520, and a two point refinement check at 1.2 million cells at about 297, totalling about 854 and rounded to 900. The dominant risk is not the arithmetic but whether the forces settle at all, which on the nearest comparable case they did not; if they do not here, the item stops early and spends far less. Graded against the measured cost afterwards per the charter's factor three rule
expected_knowledge_gain: A propeller open water curve is the most recognisable marine validation artifact after hull resistance, and unlike every other item on this line it is not blocked by the dam break gate. Three outcomes, each changing a decision. A pass gives the marine line its first passing credential and simultaneously shows that the steady moving reference frame stack can settle, which is the open question F8 left when its own gate returned no verdict because its force history never converged. A fail with settled forces bounds what the lab may claim for rotating machinery generally, not only for propellers. A no verdict on settling would be the second independent case of the same failure on this stack, converting an isolated F8 anomaly into a characterised instrument defect, which is worth more than the propeller curve itself and is why the settling test is written into the gate rather than left to judgement
hard_criterion_note: Filed as no-case after checking. It was drafted as existing-family on the assumption that the F8 rotor family carried over; that assumption does not survive contact with F8's record. F8 is a wind turbine in air whose steady branch is closed with zero gated numbers, its blade surface has no generator, and its torque sign is inverted relative to a propeller. What transfers is dictionaries and process discipline, which is not a family

launch_prompt: Propeller open-water curve, PPTC VP1304, on simpleFoam plus MRF. NOT blocked by the F7a ladder - this is single-phase and submerged - so this is the naval item that can proceed first. Step 1, zero compute: read demo-output/website/campaign/F8_MRF_HAND2001_GATE.md in full, especially its settling failure and its pre-registered averaging window, then NAVAL_CAPABILITY_GAP_MAP.md and F7a_REGATE_SPEC.md. Step 2, zero compute: obtain SVA Report 3752, hash it, and identify all four corrected open-water tables; the pre-registration must name ONE by its correction, quoting the report's own description of it, and must state why that one. Do not proceed while the reference is a document rather than a table. Step 3: write the pre-registration - advance ratios, integration patches including whether hub and shaft count, sign conventions, KT/KQ/eta formulae written out, averaging window, transient-rejection rule, settling test, tolerance and its anchor. Step 4: geometry and mesh; the blade STL is new work, not an F8 edit. Step 5: one feasibility advance ratio, and STOP if the force history does not settle - report NO VERDICT and the instrument finding rather than sweeping. Step 6: the curve. Step 7: two-point mesh check. Budget 900 core-min with a hard stop at each stage boundary; setsid, launch_solve.sh registered, collector armed, nothing left running. Record: evidence file in demo-output/website/campaign/, birth certificate per docs/standards/MESH_STANDARD.md section 6, docket update, honest verdict.
